by_task.when: Arizona is allowable and an owned asset fits a specifically enumerated Arizona personal-property or homestead category.
by_task.procedure: Include the matching specific subsection even when the asset value exceeds its statutory dollar limit; the limit affects exempt value, not EC eligibility. Prefer the specific enumerated category, such as musical instruments, firearms, motor vehicles, or homesteads, over a broader household label.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not include a subsection when its asset category or use condition is absent, and do not list limitation or availability provisions as asset exemptions.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and an owned asset satisfies the property category and use conditions of a subsection in 11 U.S.C. § 522(d).
by_task.procedure: Include the category-specific subsection even when the asset value exceeds its dollar limit. A cap limits protected value; it does not make an otherwise matching asset ineligible.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not include a subsection when its property category or required use is absent, and do not stretch § 522(d)(3) to firearms or other property outside its listed categories.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and an owned asset satisfies the property category and use conditions of a capped subsection in 11 U.S.C. § 522(d).
by_task.procedure: Report the subsection and cap the claim rather than using the asset's full value: § 522(d)(2) at $4,450, § 522(d)(3) at $700 per particular item, § 522(d)(4) at $1,875 per debtor, and § 522(d)(6) at $2,800.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use an aggregate ceiling as the value of one item, do not omit a matching subsection merely because value exceeds its cap, and do not apply a listed category to an asset outside that category.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are an allowable namespace and the facts establish the debtor's ownership of an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Test 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) independently for every such asset because it covers any property. Include it alongside every matching category-specific exemption; its dollar limit restricts value, not EC eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it when Federal is not allowable or ownership is not established, and do not list § 522(b), § 522(d), or § 522(m) as asset exemptions.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and the facts establish the debtor's ownership and value of an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Report 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) once as an independent alternative alongside every matching category-specific exemption. For this independent alternative, treat § 522(d)(1) as unused even if a residence exists or a separate alternative lists § 522(d)(1). Claim the lesser of the asset value and $15,425 for one debtor; for jointly owned property in a joint case, apply § 522(m) separately to both equal interests, up to $30,850 total.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it when Federal is not allowable or ownership is not established, do not subtract claims made under separate asset-exemption alternatives, and do not report § 522(m), § 522(b), or § 522(d) as an asset exemption.

by_task.when: Illinois is allowable and the facts establish ownership of personal property used for personal rather than business purposes.
by_task.procedure: Test 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently for that property and include it alongside any matching specific exemption, such as wearing apparel, a motor vehicle, or a prescribed health aid. Its dollar limit does not determine EC eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it to real-property homesteads, property not owned by the debtor, or property used for business rather than personal purposes; do not substitute a tools-of-trade or homestead citation merely because the item is useful in a home.

by_task.when: Illinois is allowable and the facts establish the value and ownership of personal property used for personal rather than business purposes.
by_task.procedure: Report 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) as an independent alternative alongside every matching specific exemption. Claim the lesser of value and $4,000 for one debtor; in a joint case, apply the $4,000 exemption to each spouse's equal interest, permitting up to $8,000 total.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it to real-property homesteads, unowned property, or business-use property, and do not replace a separately matching specific exemption.

by_task.when: Oregon is an allowable namespace and the owned asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: Report Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) once as an independent alternative in addition to any specific Oregon exemption. Claim the asset value when it is $400 or less and $400 when it is greater.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit it because a vehicle, household, apparel, jewelry, or firearm exemption also applies, and do not apply it to real-property homesteads or homestead-sale proceeds.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania is allowable and the facts establish the debtor's ownership of estate property.
by_task.procedure: Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 once as an independent general monetary alternative for every owned item, whether real or personal and regardless of value, alongside every matching Federal or specific Pennsylvania exemption.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit it because value exceeds its monetary limit. Do not replace it with § 8124(a); § 8124(a)(1) requires wearing apparel and does not cover vehicles, firearms, or general household property.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania is allowable and the facts establish the debtor's ownership and value of estate property.
by_task.procedure: Report 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 independently for every owned item. For one debtor claim the lesser of value and $300. For equal jointly owned property in a joint case, claim the lesser of total value and $600.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use $300 for jointly owned property worth at least $600, do not report a ceiling above the asset's value, and do not substitute § 8124(a)(1) unless the property is wearing apparel.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and an owned asset satisfies the property category and use conditions of a subsection in 11 U.S.C. § 522(d).
by_task.procedure: Include the category-specific subsection even when the asset value exceeds its dollar limit. A cap limits protected value; it does not make an otherwise matching asset ineligible.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not include a subsection when its property category or required use is absent, and do not stretch § 522(d)(3) to firearms or other property outside its listed categories.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and an owned asset satisfies the property category and use conditions of a capped subsection in 11 U.S.C. § 522(d).
by_task.procedure: Report the matching subsection and cap each independent claim. Use the lesser of value and $4,450 under § 522(d)(2), $700 for each particular item under § 522(d)(3), and $2,800 under § 522(d)(6). Under § 522(d)(4), use the lesser of value and $1,875 for one debtor; for jointly owned jewelry in a joint case, apply $1,875 to each equal interest and sum, up to $3,750.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use an aggregate ceiling or the full asset value for one § 522(d)(3) item, even in a joint case. Do not treat jewelry as § 522(d)(3), or apply any listed category to firearms or other property outside that category.

operations.rationale: The remaining errors are category-cap amount errors, not missing eligibility rules: the parent used full values under § 522(d)(3), failed to combine the per-debtor jewelry limit in a joint case, and sometimes treated a cap as excluding an otherwise matching item.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are an allowable namespace and the facts establish the debtor's ownership of an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Test 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) independently for every such asset because it covers any property. After testing specific categories, make a separate per-asset pass and include § 522(d)(5) once for every owned asset, including property with a specific exemption.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it when Federal is not allowable or ownership is not established, and do not list § 522(b), § 522(d), or § 522(m) as asset exemptions.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and the facts establish the debtor's ownership and value of an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Report 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) once for every owned asset as an independent alternative. Treat § 522(d)(1) as unused for this alternative. For one debtor claim the lesser of value and $15,425. For equal jointly owned property in a joint case, compute the lesser of half the value and $15,425 for each spouse and add the two amounts, equivalently the lesser of total value and $30,850.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 522(d)(5) because a category-specific exemption also applies, do not subtract claims listed as separate alternatives, and do not report § 522(m), § 522(b), or § 522(d) as an asset exemption.

operations.rationale: Current predictions still omit the wildcard from some owned assets and use the single-debtor amount for joint property. This update separates the missing-law completeness pass from the joint-case arithmetic correction.

by_task.when: Illinois is allowable and the facts establish ownership of personal property used for personal rather than business purposes, applying the task's personal-use default unless the facts expressly state actual business use.
by_task.procedure: Test 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently for every such item and include it alongside any matching specific exemption, including wearing apparel, a motor vehicle, or a prescribed health aid.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not infer business use merely from words such as business, professional, work, tool, or appliance in an item's description. Do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel or household items as tools of trade without the required facts; do not apply this personal-property rule to a real-property homestead or unowned property.

by_task.when: Illinois is allowable and the facts establish the value and ownership of personal property used for personal rather than business purposes, applying the task's personal-use default unless actual business use is expressly stated.
by_task.procedure: Report 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently alongside every matching specific exemption. Claim the lesser of value and $4,000 for one debtor. For equal jointly owned property in a joint case, claim the lesser of total value and $8,000.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not report the $4,000 ceiling when the asset is worth less, do not infer business use from a descriptive label alone, and do not replace a separately matching specific exemption or apply the rule to real-property homesteads or unowned property.

operations.rationale: The parent continues to treat the wildcard as displaced by specific exemptions, infer business use from labels, and report a ceiling rather than the lesser asset value. Joint cases also require the supplied per-spouse total rather than a single $4,000 cap.

by_task.avoid_when: Do not let a specific Oregon category displace § 18.345(1)(p), and do not apply it to real-property homesteads or homestead-sale proceeds.

operations.rationale: The unresolved Oregon error is omission of the general personal-property alternative when a specific exemption is already present, including on vehicles and ordinary household or apparel property; the $400 amount rule itself remains unchanged.

by_task.when: Arizona is allowable and an owned asset fits a specifically enumerated Arizona personal-property or homestead category.
by_task.procedure: Include the matching specific subsection even when the asset value exceeds its statutory dollar limit; the limit affects exempt value, not EC eligibility. Prefer the specific enumerated category, such as musical instruments, firearms, motor vehicles, or homesteads, over a broader household label. Treat clothing as wearing apparel despite work-related wording. Treat a professionally prescribed assistive device supporting mobility or communication as a prosthetic device under § 33-1125(9).
by_task.avoid_when: Do not include a subsection when its asset category or use condition is absent, and do not list limitation or availability provisions as asset exemptions. Section 33-1125(4) covers engagement and wedding rings, not anniversary rings or other jewelry.

by_task.when: Arizona is allowable and an owned asset fits a specifically enumerated Arizona category and its value is established.
by_task.procedure: Report the matching specific subsection and use the lesser of value and any stated statutory cap. For a qualifying professionally prescribed assistive or prosthetic device under § 33-1125(9), which states no dollar cap, report the full asset value.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not treat an anniversary ring or other jewelry as an engagement or wedding ring under § 33-1125(4), and do not omit a prescribed mobility or communication aid merely because the statute gives examples rather than an exhaustive device list.

operations.rationale: Arizona failures concern distinct category boundaries: work-related wording did not negate apparel, an anniversary ring was falsely treated as an engagement or wedding ring, and a prescribed communication aid was omitted from the prosthetic-device category in both tasks.
